rationale: TASD/TASDER decomposes unstructured sparse tensors into structured-sparse tensor algebra and proposes dataflow/architectural support, with a real RTX 3080 sparse-tensor-core demonstration. Because the work is partly a hardware/dataflow framework rather than a standalone software kernel, it is borderline but still centered on accelerator-level sparse execution.

VoLUT is a volumetric-video streaming system using dilated interpolation, LUT-based super-resolution refinement, and ABR adaptation. The contributions are application-level SR and streaming pipeline design rather than compute kernels.

FLStore unifies data and compute planes for federated-learning metadata/non-training workloads via a serverless cache and tailored caching policies. It is a storage and execution framework above the kernel layer.

TurboAttention enables quantized execution of attention through FlashQ headwise quantization, mixed-precision KV cache, and SAS softmax approximation implemented with Triton attention kernels. The stated goal is quantized attention computation rather than only KV-cache compression.

QServe/QoQ is a W4A8KV4 quantization and serving co-design with CUDA/PTX kernels, efficient dequantization, compute-aware weight reordering, and accelerated KV4 attention. The precision format and its kernel support are central contributions.
